title: Teldrassil
body: Teldrassil, whose name means crown of the earth, is the second World Tree of the night elves, rising from the Veiled Sea northwest of Darkshore. After the Battle of Mount Hyjal left Nordrassil scarred and the kaldorei mortal, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm won the approval of the Circle of Ancients and, with the most powerful druids, grew this new tree in the hope of winning their immortality back. Its upper boughs hold a whole forested land of hills, lakes and streams. Darnassus stands in the west, the village of Dolanaar sits beside the road, the young begin their training in the twilit glade of Shadowglen, and Rut'theran Village at the roots links the island to the mainland. Yet the tree was grown without a blessing. Nozdormu refused one, rebuking Staghelm for his arrogance, and Alexstrasza followed him. Since then Teldrassil's growth has been flawed and unpredictable. Corrupted fel cones drop from its branches, the gentle Gnarlpine furbolgs have turned savage, sick and angry timberlings rise from the soil, and satyrs lurk in its hollows.

title: Shadowglen
body: Ringed by mountains in the northeast of Teldrassil, Shadowglen is a small twilit glade open only to the south, where the road runs down toward Dolanaar. Here young night elves first take up blade, bow and staff under mentors who wait inside the great tree Aldrassil. Even this sheltered place feels the tree's troubles. Conservator Ilthalaine reports that heavy spring rains let the nightsabers and thistle boars multiply beyond what the glade can feed, and grells and grellkin tainted by fel moss creep through the woods. North of Aldrassil lies a moonwell, and a phial of its water is the first step of the long lesson Tenaron Stormgrip sets for every pupil.

title: Aldrassil
body: At the heart of Shadowglen rises Aldrassil, a great tree within the World Tree, its hollow levels home to the trainers who teach each new generation of night elf warriors, hunters, rogues, priests and druids. Sigils sent from inside its walls call the young to their first lessons, reminding them that their people have rejoined the other races of Azeroth and now need protectors of every kind. Mardant Strongoak guides young druids near the top of the tree, and the highest room belongs to Tenaron Stormgrip, who leads Shadowglen. A visiting scholar, Gilshalan Windwalker, works here too, studying the webwood spiders to learn how the new tree has changed them.

title: Shadowthread Cave
body: On the northern edge of Shadowglen opens the Shadowthread Cave, a lair of webwood spiders. They are cousins of a far smaller breed, and Gilshalan Windwalker believes the growth of the new World Tree has swollen them to their present size; he seeks their venom and an egg from the nest deep inside to prove it. The cave is a real danger to the careless. The young elf Iverron wandered too close and was badly bitten by a spider called Githyiss the Vile, and only an antidote brewed by his friend Dirania Silvershine, from hyacinth mushrooms, moonpetal lilies and the spiders' own ichor, set him on the mend.

title: Starbreeze Village
body: Starbreeze was a quiet hamlet of a few small night elf houses near a moonwell in eastern Teldrassil, southeast of Shadowglen and east of Dolanaar. That peace ended when the Gnarlpine furbolgs, maddened by fel moss, ambushed Gaerolas Talvethren, Great Warden of the sleeping Druids of the Talon, as he left for the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, and then pillaged the village. Gaerolas still lingers there, too badly wounded to carry the news himself. Gnarlpine warriors, gardeners and ursas now roam among the homes, among them a dangerous brute called Uruson. When the village fell, Tallonkai Swiftroot had to leave a treasured emerald dreamcatcher behind in his dresser.

title: Dolanaar
body: Dolanaar is the first true town on the road south from Shadowglen, a night elf village in central Teldrassil gathered about a moonwell. Its inn offers rest under Elune's watch, and its trainers carry on the lessons begun at Aldrassil. It is also where the troubles of the forest are weighed. Corithras Moonrage tends the moonwell and tells the story of the tree's making, the druid Athridas Bearmantle watches over the slumbering Druids of the Talon, and Tallonkai Swiftroot quietly wants a satyr lord hiding just to the north put down. Sentinels keep watch over the village, and Moon Priestess Amara watches the road west to Darnassus.

title: Fel Rock
body: Just north of Dolanaar lies Fel Rock, a cave whose old beauty has given way to corruption. The satyr Lord Melenas has made it his lair and gathered a large band of grell warriors about him, joined by shadow, rascal and dark sprites, and a rare, brutish grell called Threggil prowls among them. In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot treats Melenas as a shameful secret, a satyr far too close to home, and asks those he sends into the cave to settle the matter quickly and quietly.

title: Lake Al'Ameth
body: South of Dolanaar spreads Lake Al'Ameth, one of the largest lakes on Teldrassil. Its shores have grown unsafe, for the timberlings, elementals of nature that mirror the health of the tree's plants and animals, have turned angry, and diseased sprouts keep springing up along the water. The herbalist Denalan keeps a small camp on the eastern shore with a planter of specially prepared soil, testing seeds, fronds and fruit in search of a cure. In a cave on the southern bank lurks Oakenscowl, once a grand leader among the timberlings, now swollen by the largest tumor Denalan has ever seen and spreading corruption to every creature of the lake.

title: Ban'ethil Hollow
body: West of Dolanaar, below the road to Darnassus, lies Ban'ethil Hollow. It now belongs to the Gnarlpine, whose shamans, augurs and defenders crowd its slopes, while ambushers creep up from their den to fall on travelers bound for the capital. News and trade pass along that road every day, and the Sentinels of Teldrassil reward anyone who thins the ambushers' ranks. Somewhere within the hollow lies the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, a sacred resting place of the Druids of the Talon that the furbolgs have overrun.

title: Ban'ethil Barrow Den
body: The Ban'ethil Barrow Den is one of the sacred places the night elves built to shelter the Druids of the Talon while they sleep, their spirits walking the Emerald Dream in keeping with a pact with Ysera. Its keepers stored the Relics of Wakening, a talisman, a quill, a sapphire and a rune, in chests within, for the hibernation cannot be broken safely without them. Gnarlpine invaders have since ransacked the den. Their shamans have even learned to part a sleeping druid's spirit from his body: the spirit of Oben Rageclaw wanders the barrow, powerless, while his own animated form guards its deepest chambers against intruders.

title: Gnarlpine Hold
body: In the far southwest of Teldrassil lies Gnarlpine Hold, home of the Gnarlpine furbolgs. They were once a peaceful people and friends of the night elves, but fel moss has driven them mad, and here their chieftain Ursal the Mauler uses its evil power to keep his tribe in a frenzy. Pathfinders, avengers and totemics guard the hold, along with a hulking brute named Grimmaw. Druids of the Talon carried off from the Ban'ethil Barrow Den are held captive here under Ursal's curse, and only his death can set them free.

title: Pools of Arlithrien
body: The Pools of Arlithrien are a scatter of small pools in western Teldrassil, just southeast of the entrance to Darnassus. Once a peaceful spot, they are now prowled by nightsaber stalkers and webwood spiders, and the Gnarlpine have pressed so close that the Sentinels struggle to patrol the area. A lone moonwell still stands on the shore. Its water is still needed by the druids of Darnassus, but those who come to fill a phial are warned to keep their weapons close at hand.

title: Wellspring Lake
body: Southeast of the Oracle Glade and northeast of Darnassus, Wellspring Lake is fed by a spring deep within the World Tree and drains away along the Wellspring River. The night elves once came here to fish, but the timberlings that wander its waters are the most tainted on the island, studded with mossy tumors full of poison, and the druids have ordered them cut down so the tumors can be burned. Along the river gather elder timberlings and mire beasts, and among them moves Blackmoss the Fetid, whose heart, sheathed in dark and oily moss, keeps beating even after he falls.

title: The Oracle Glade
body: In the northwest of Teldrassil stands the Oracle Tree, an ancient and wise presence that watches over the growth of Teldrassil alongside the druids and sends its reports to the Arch Druid on shed pieces of inscribed bark. Beneath its boughs lies the first and most powerful moonwell on the island. Bloodfeather harpies have built their nests all around the glade, and when the tree sent a runner to Darnassus, the harpies killed the messenger. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak and a small band of Sentinels hold the moonwell and push the harpies back little by little. On a branch at the glade's edge dwells the reclusive satyr Sethir the Ancient.

title: Rut'theran Village
body: Rut'theran Village sits among the roots of Teldrassil on the shore of the Veiled Sea, the island's link to the mainland. A portal carries travelers up to Darnassus, a ferry sails to Auberdine in Darkshore, and hippogryphs fly constantly between the village and the far shore, while Erelas Ambersky trains and cares for the young birds. The waters here are astonishingly rich. Fish caught off Teldrassil grow to nearly twice the size of their mainland kin, and Nessa Shadowsong and the other villagers suspect the swift growth of the World Tree itself. Daryn Lightwind, a lore keeper of the Cenarion Circle, keeps her piles of books here, among them a history of Feralas.

title: Tenaron Stormgrip
body: Tenaron Stormgrip leads Shadowglen from the highest room atop Aldrassil, and he summons each promising young night elf before they set out into the wider world. He holds that none should leave the enchanted forests without first understanding their people's recent history: the Battle of Mount Hyjal, Nordrassil left a pale shadow after its power was spent against Archimonde, and the moonwells that hold the waters of the ancient Well of Eternity, which the druids use and the Sentinels revere, though sorcery stays forbidden to all. He begins that lesson with a single phial from the moonwell north of Aldrassil, then sends his pupils south to Corithras Moonrage.

title: Corithras Moonrage
body: Corithras Moonrage tends the moonwell of Dolanaar and carries on the telling that Tenaron Stormgrip begins. He sends young messengers to the moonwells of Starbreeze Village, the Pools of Arlithrien and the Oracle Glade, and repays each phial with another chapter: immortality lost after Hyjal, the Betrayer freed, Malfurion Stormrage vanished, and Fandral Staghelm persuading the Circle of Ancients to grow a new World Tree. He does not hide what went wrong. The dragons withheld their blessing, and he speaks plainly of the flawed growth, strange beasts and crazed furbolgs that trouble the night elves' new home, before pouring the waters together for the Arch Druid in Darnassus.

title: Athridas Bearmantle
body: The druid Athridas Bearmantle of Dolanaar shares the dryad Tarindrella's concern for the well being of the forest, and he keeps watch over his brethren the Druids of the Talon, who slumber in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den with their spirits in the Emerald Dream. When word from their warden Gaerolas Talvethren was late in coming, he grew uneasy and sent help, and what came back was grave news: the Gnarlpine had been corrupted and the barrow ravaged. Athridas set himself to prepare the ritual of awakening with the recovered Relics of Wakening, knowing it could take effect only once Ursal the Mauler, who had meddled with the sleepers, was slain.

title: Tarindrella
body: Tarindrella is a dryad, a mysterious woodland protector whose presence had not been felt in the forests of Kalimdor for years. Her sudden return to Shadowglen, southwest of Aldrassil, reached the druid Melithar Staghelm through the whisperings of the forest spirits, and he took it as a sure sign that something was amiss. She had come because of a gathering evil. The peaceful furbolgs of the hills were deserting their homes and massing as the Gnarlpine tribe, and she suspected the wicked fel moss. When the grells of Shadowglen proved to be tainted by it, her fears were confirmed, and she pointed the way to Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar, who shares her concern.

title: Denalan
body: Denalan is a night elf herbalist who has pitched his camp on the eastern shore of Lake Al'Ameth to study the plant life of Teldrassil. The tree's creation was a grand achievement, he says, but now the world must shift to regain its balance. Believing the soil itself is what angers the timberlings, he works with rare earths sent from Darnassus and a planter of specially prepared soil, and he tests strange plants, one like nothing he has seen since a journey to the Swamp of Sorrows decades ago. He shares his work with the druid Rellian Greenspyre of Darnassus, who believes Denalan may be the timberlings' only hope.

title: Zenn Foulhoof
body: Zenn Foulhoof is a satyr who lingers on the outskirts of Dolanaar, all charm and promises of things beyond imagining for any young night elf willing to run his errands. What he wants are fangs, feathers and silk taken from the creatures of the forest, reagents for his secret business, and once he has them he crows his thanks to the naive and gullible. The Council of the Forest takes a dim view of anyone who helps him. To redeem themselves, his helpers are told to bring him fel cones, the corrupted seeds that fall smoking from the trees, as a harmless looking snack. One taste turns Zenn into a croaking frog.

title: Ursal the Mauler
body: Ursal the Mauler is the chieftain of the Gnarlpine furbolgs, ruling them from Gnarlpine Hold in the southwest of Teldrassil. It is Ursal who wields the evil power of fel moss to drive his once peaceful tribe into madness, and under him the furbolgs ambushed the warden Gaerolas Talvethren, pillaged Starbreeze Village and invaded the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. He meddled with the calling of the sleeping Druids of the Talon and holds several of them captive at his hold. The druids of Dolanaar have concluded that the ritual to wake their brethren cannot succeed while he lives, and when he falls, his captives wake and cry out that the nightmare is over.

title: Lord Melenas
body: Satyrs are an old shame to the night elves, and Lord Melenas is a shame far too close to home. From the cave of Fel Rock, just north of Dolanaar, this vicious satyr has gathered a large band of grell warriors, and his heart is said to be black as night as he plots something foul. Tallonkai Swiftroot of Dolanaar would rather the matter stayed between trusted friends. He asks that Melenas be dealt with quickly and quietly, before more is made of it, and wants only the satyr's head as proof that the embarrassment is ended.

title: Oben Rageclaw
body: Oben Rageclaw was a druid of the Claw who slept in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den when the Gnarlpine came. Their shamans have discovered how to separate a sleeping druid's spirit from his body, and they did so to Oben, animating his empty form and turning it against anyone who explores the den. His spirit lingers in the barrow, trapped in the Emerald Dream and powerless to stop it. After studying one of the shamans' voodoo charms, he saw only one way out: his own body must be slain and the charm used upon it, so that his spirit may at last rest peacefully in the Dream.
sources: quest 2541 description (shamans separate spirit from body, animated form attacks explorers, trapped in the Emerald Dream)
quest 2561 description and reward (kill my physical form, use the charm, rest peacefully in the Emerald Dream)

title: Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak
body: Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak was sent with a small group of Sentinels to protect the sanctity of the Oracle Glade from the Bloodfeather harpies nesting all around it. She holds her post at the moonwell beneath the Oracle Tree and drives the harpies back a little at a time. Her loss was a personal one as well. Her gray sabercat companion Mist was taken when the harpy witches caught Arynia off guard, and she blamed herself, believing Mist dead. The cat lived, though cruelly wounded, and found her own way back with a stranger's help. Arynia's joy at the reunion is matched only by her gratitude.
sources: quest_greeting 3519 (tasked with protecting the sanctity of the Oracle Grove)
quest 937 description (small group of Sentinels, push the harpies back)
quest 938 description, request and reward texts (gray sabercat, badly wounded, the witches caught me off guard, eternal gratitude)

title: Sethir the Ancient
body: High on a branch at the edge of the Oracle Glade lives Sethir the Ancient, a reclusive satyr whom the rogues of Darnassus believe may understand what is happening to the forests of Teldrassil. Every attempt to approach him, by force or by diplomacy, has ended in death, and he warns intruders that they will join the others at the bottom of the world tree. Alone, he rants of filth everywhere and of forests that must be cleansed, and despairs that cutting one growth down only brings two more. The journal he carries, written in a script no one can read, points to the same sickness that has already gripped the forests of Darkshore.
sources: quest 2242 description (one being who may help understand, hides on a branch at the outskirts of the Oracle Glade, all who approached met with doom)
quest 2242 reward text (the sickness which has gripped Darkshore has begun to taint our home)
creature_text 6909 (I know you are there... bottom of the world tree; Filth everywhere; cutting one down results in two new growths)
item 7737 Sethir's Journal (written in a language you cannot decipher)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Sethir_the_Ancient
notes: Faction 0: Sethir uses faction template 14, hostile to all players, reachable by Horde as for Ursal. Quests 2241 and 2242 are left free for Darnassus. Verified.

title: Crown of the Earth
body: Before the young of Shadowglen go out into the world, they are sent to learn how their new home came to be. Tenaron Stormgrip asks for water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil and sends it on to Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar, who dispatches the messenger in turn to the moonwells of Starbreeze Village, the Pools of Arlithrien and finally the Oracle Glade, home of the first and most powerful well. With each phial comes another part of the tale. After Hyjal the night elves lost their immortality and Malfurion vanished, so Fandral Staghelm, with the Circle of Ancients' approval, grew Teldrassil to win it back. But when he sought the dragons' blessing, Nozdormu refused him for his arrogance and Alexstrasza agreed, and the tree has grown flawed ever since. The waters, poured together, are carried at last to the Arch Druid, whose druids in Darnassus need them to replenish their own moonwell.
sources: quests 920, 921, 928, 929, 933, 7383, 935 (descriptions, request and reward texts)
quest 929 description (the druids in Darnassus use moonwell water, their moonwell must be replenished)
notes: Chain 920 > 921 > 928 > 929 > 933 > 7383 > 935. Quest 934 is an unused duplicate of 7383 with no giver. The final quest 935 is turned in to Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus and is left free as a trigger for the Darnassus writer. Verified.

title: The Sleepers of Ban'ethil
body: The first sign came to Shadowglen, where the dryad Tarindrella returned to find the grells tainted by fel moss and feared for the Gnarlpine furbolgs. In Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle had his own worry: no word had come from Gaerolas Talvethren, Great Warden of the Druids of the Talon who sleep in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, bound by a pact with Ysera. Gaerolas was found wounded at Starbreeze Village. The Gnarlpine had ambushed him and sacked the village, maddened by their chieftain Ursal the Mauler and his fel moss. Worse, they had ravaged the barrow and carried off sleeping druids, who would stay lost in the Dream forever unless woken. The four Relics of Wakening were recovered from the den's sacred chests so Athridas could prepare the ritual, but it could take hold only once Ursal fell at Gnarlpine Hold. With his death, the captive druids woke and cried out that they were free.
sources: quests 458, 459 (Tarindrella, Fel Moss, grells, Athridas)
quests 475, 476, 483, 486 (descriptions, request and reward texts)
creature_text 2852
notes: Two entry points: 458 in Shadowglen (Melithar Staghelm, leading through 459 to Athridas) and 475 in Dolanaar. Verified.

title: The Tainted Timberlings
body: The timberlings of Teldrassil mirror the health of its plants and beasts, and they have grown angry. Denalan, camped on Lake Al'Ameth, suspects the soil, and with rare earths from Darnassus he plants seeds gathered from the lake's timberlings in hope of growing a gentler generation, while the sickly sprouts along the shore are pulled up before they can grow. One seed goes to the druid Rellian Greenspyre, who finds that the parents' taint passes into their seeds and orders the worst afflicted, those of Wellspring Lake, cut down and their mossy tumors burned. Denalan at last traces the spreading corruption to Oakenscowl, once a noble timberling leader, now bloated by a gargantuan tumor in a cave on the lake's southern bank. Even the heart of Blackmoss the Fetid, scraped of its oily moss, looks much like a seed, and from Denalan's soil it emerges cleansed.
sources: quests 997, 918, 919, 922, 923, 2498, 2499 (descriptions, request and reward texts)
quests 927, 941 and creature_text 2080 (heart looks like a seed, planted, emerges cleansed)
notes: 'Proves to be a seed' softened to what Denalan says (it looks like a seed). Otherwise verified; 922, 923, 2498 left free for Darnassus.

title: The Emerald Dreamcatcher
body: Tallonkai Swiftroot of Dolanaar was once given an emerald dreamcatcher by Gaerolas Talvethren, warden of the sleeping druids, a gift granted to few: an amulet able to draw energy from the Emerald Dream and bring luck to whoever carries it. When the Gnarlpine overran Starbreeze Village, the dreamcatcher was left behind in Tallonkai's dresser there. It came back damaged, its emerald gone. Reports soon placed the stone with Ferocitas the Dream Eater, leader of a band of Gnarlpine mystics north of Starbreeze, who had been seen wearing a necklace that glowed green in the night. The jewel's power was useless to the furbolg, but Tallonkai would not rest until his gift was whole, and the mystics paid for the theft as the emerald was taken back.
sources: quest 2438 description and reward text (gift from Gaerolas, siphons energy from the Emerald Dream, luck, dresser in Starbreeze, a gift only given to few)
quest 2459 description (emerald missing, Ferocitas north of Starbreeze, necklace glows green, power useless to him, kill mystics)
DB: Ferocitas 7234 and Gnarlpine Mystic 7235 spawns north of Starbreeze
notes: Chain 2438 > 2459. Verified.

title: The Oracle's Messenger
body: The Oracle Tree has watched over Teldrassil's growth beside the druids, sending its reports to the Arch Druid in Darnassus. Then the reports stopped. Bloodfeather harpies had nested all around its glade, and when the tree sent a runner to the capital, the harpies cut the messenger down. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak and her small band could only push them back a little at a time until help came, and the harpies were driven from their nests. As they fled, the tree felt a greater calm spread across the forest and its creatures feel safe once more. It shed a piece of inscribed bark bearing its report and entrusted it to the one who had freed the glade, promising that the forest would see the bearer safely along its paths. In Darnassus the Arch Druid read the report as a sign that some of Teldrassil's troubles were easing while others grew worse.
sources: quest 937 description and reward text (harpies, runner killed, the Oracle Tree shed a piece of its bark)
quest 940 description and reward text (greater calm spread, forest will see you safely, some problems lessened while others grow)
quest 940 start item 5219 Inscribed Bark
notes: Chain 937 > 940 > 952. 940 is turned in to Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus and is left free as a trigger for the Darnassus writer; 952 continues to Onu in Darkshore. Mist (938) is covered under Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak. Verified.
